perOption.label: A
perOption.reason: 'based' is a reduced relative clause modifying 'Environmental taxes' ('taxes [that are] based directly on measured emissions'). The finite verb slot is already filled by 'can be targeted', so a participle is required, and the passive participle is right since taxes are what get based on emissions. Distractor pull: misreading 'based' as the main verb and wanting 'are based' — but 'can' already serves as the finite verb.

perOption.label: B
perOption.reason: 'incentive + to-infinitive' ('an incentive to reduce emissions') is the canonical complementation pattern. No alternative parse makes it wrong.

perOption.label: C
perOption.reason: Head of the subject is 'The great attraction' (singular); 'of basing the tax directly on measured emissions' is a prepositional modifier. Singular 'is' is correct. Classic proximity trap: plural 'emissions' immediately before the verb tempts 'are', but the printed 'is' is exactly right.

perOption.label: D
perOption.reason: 'particularly which there are many separate sources of emissions' fails every parse: as a relative pronoun 'which' needs an antecedent and a gap in its clause, but 'there are many separate sources of emissions' is a complete existential clause with no gap and no plausible antecedent; 'which' cannot head a free relative in standard English; a sentential relative also requires a gap. The context requires the adverbial subordinator 'where' (or 'when'): 'particularly where there are many separate sources of emissions'. Ungrammatical — this is the answer.

perOption.label: E
perOption.reason: Head noun of the long subject is 'technologies' (plural), so 'have' agrees across the modifier 'available for monitoring ... in waste discharges'. Intransitive 'develop' (= advance/improve) makes active 'have been developing' correct; the tempting 'error' reading ('should be passive have been developed') fails because technologies develop on their own in this sense. Most seductive distractor for a rushed solver, but fully grammatical.

note: Clean item. Exactly one ungrammatical underline (D: relative pronoun 'which' where adverbial 'where' is required — no gap, no antecedent). The other four are well-formed with genuine long-distance traps (C: proximity-plural before singular verb; E: long subject agreement + active/passive temptation with 'develop'; A: participle vs. finite verb). Actively searched for rescuing parses of (D) — free relative, sentential relative — none succeed. Single defensible answer.
